nodes.label: KMPART1 Paper Parts

nodes.label: KMPART2 Paper Parts (cid, length, part_checksum)

nodes.label: KMSHARE1 Share Record (42 bytes)
nodes.rationale: 4-byte set id, k, index, 32-byte value, 4-byte checksum; prefix avoids KEYM collision. Reader frozen.

nodes.label: KMSHARE2 Share Record (66 bytes)
nodes.rationale: Widens set id and checksum to 128 bits for decades-long archival identity; envelope-only change; new sets written as KMSHARE2, readers accept both.

nodes.label: Set Code (XXXX-XXXX)
nodes.rationale: First 40 bits of share_set_id_v2 in base32, a human label matching the start of every KMSHARE2 strip; not a check.

nodes.label: share_set_id (derived from slot_salt)

nodes.label: lp() length-prefix encoding (4.1)
nodes.rationale: Length prefixes make the concatenation injective so no two field sequences collide.

nodes.label: Final-chunk flag truncation defence
nodes.rationale: Final chunk uses a different nonce flag byte, so a truncated container fails rather than decrypting to a valid-looking prefix.

nodes.label: Skip unattemptable slots, never reject (4.4)
nodes.rationale: A share slot or Argon2id slot beside a usable passphrase slot must not make the file unopenable; failure only reported once the slot table is exhausted.

nodes.label: Master Key Wrap (constant wrap nonce)
nodes.rationale: Nonce is 11 zero bytes then 0xFF, not slot index, so removing a slot never forces re-wrapping others (which needs their secrets); 0xFF keeps it outside payload nonce space.

nodes.label: KM-14 Missing Parameter Bounds

nodes.label: Master Key (envelope key)
nodes.rationale: 32 random bytes per container; re-passwording does not touch payload, nonces no longer depend on salt freshness, splicing resists salt-reuse bugs.

nodes.label: Passkey / WebAuthn PRF Slot (slot_type 0x01)
nodes.rationale: prf_salt derived from slot_salt and discoverable credential used so no variable-length field is needed; not archival (bound to RP id), never the only slot, adds convenience and phishing resistance not strength.

nodes.label: Passphrase-and-Shares Slot (slot_type 0x03)
nodes.rationale: Estate case: needs both passphrase and k shares. Passphrase stretched by slot KDF first, then combined with share secret via HKDF; may be the only slot.

nodes.label: SEAL/OPEN per cipher_id (incl. chained)
nodes.rationale: Same SEAL used for chunks and slot wraps so a chained container's wrap is chained too.

nodes.label: Shamir Share Set Slot (slot_type 0x02)
nodes.rationale: Slot secret reconstructed from k paper shares; share_secret never stored; each share as sensitive as the password.

nodes.label: Shamir Split (per-byte polynomials, indices 1..n)
nodes.rationale: Sequential indices make shares referable; n not stored in share record.

nodes.label: Slot Key
nodes.rationale: Derived per slot from slot secret, salt and params; unwraps the master key.

nodes.label: STREAM Nonces and Final-Chunk Flag
nodes.rationale: uint88 counter || final flag (age-style); safe because master key is fresh per container; final flag makes truncation detectable.

nodes.label: Freshness Rules (CSPRNG MUSTs)
nodes.rationale: master_key, slot_salt, share_secret and every Shamir coefficient per byte position fresh; reusing coefficients across positions collapses k-of-n to 1-of-n while still round-tripping.

nodes.label: KDF / slot_type Pairing Rule
nodes.rationale: Passphrase slots never HKDF (unstretched password); random-secret slots only HKDF; enforced in both directions before any KDF.

nodes.label: Master Key Confirmation via Chunk 0
nodes.rationale: A spliced foreign slot can unwrap to another container's key; readers and writers must confirm candidate by opening chunk 0 before using it.

nodes.label: Slot Amendment Cost Record
nodes.rationale: Spent fixed header, single AAD rule, failure time; gained F5 downgrade, splice resistance, re-passwording without re-encryption. Landed before any v2 container was written.

nodes.label: Passkey Is Not a Backup

nodes.label: keym2: vs KEYM1: Text Prefixes
nodes.rationale: Lowercase k separates armor from a raw binary container at byte 0.

nodes.label: Aggregate Unlock Cost (keym2UnlockCost)
nodes.rationale: 8 max-cost slots: ~41 s Argon2id, ~315 s PBKDF2. Reader MUST NOT refuse for cost; SHOULD price and warn with a Stop control.

nodes.label: Core Header (8 bytes)
nodes.rationale: Magic, version 0x02, cipher_id, flags, reserved; authenticated by every AEAD invocation.

nodes.label: Findings F6/F7: Slot-Scoped Rejection Gaps
nodes.rationale: Rules written for one unlock path became ambiguous with several.

nodes.label: Migration and Format Freeze
nodes.rationale: Frozen once users held v2 containers; frozen still admits new slot types because old readers skip them.

nodes.label: slot_count (1..8)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately outside both AADs so the table stays editable; exposure confined to denial of service. Bounded to 8 because per-slot KDF cost multiplies by it.

nodes.label: Slot Record (96/112 bytes)
nodes.rationale: 48-byte prefix (type, kdf_id, flags, reserved, 32-byte salt, 8-byte KDF params) plus wrapped key; shape unchanged for all slot types.

nodes.label: Slot Table
nodes.rationale: Mutable table of fixed-width slots; each slot authenticated only by its own wrap so slots can be added/removed holding one secret.

nodes.label: Two AADs (payload_aad and slot_aad)
nodes.rationale: Payload must be immutable, slot table mutable; both AADs are contiguous container byte ranges so implementations cannot disagree on reconstruction.

nodes.label: Fields Bounded by Format Constants
nodes.rationale: Every header field is attacker-controlled when read; a field that must exist is bounded by a constant of the format, never by another field. Header-length and plaintext-length fields removed.

nodes.label: Reject Non-Zero Reserved Fields
nodes.rationale: Reserved fields are AAD-covered so non-zero means deliberate writer intent; fail closed. Bit 0 is LSB. Scope is per attempted slot.

nodes.label: Unknown Slot Type Skip Rule
nodes.rationale: Rejecting unknown types or validating skipped slots would brick containers for older readers when new slot types are enrolled: a data-loss event. Failure only after table exhausted.
